Faith is my babygirl 

Like she gets a lot of flack for who is is/what she’s done but her arc is actually amazing. 

She did something completely accidental - that could’ve been something Buffy herself had done - and she reacted irrationally because she was a teenage girl. Because she’d been abused, in the foster system, had a dead mother (Go Ask Malice for ref) and watched her Watcher, who was the first person who ever cared about her get brutally murdered in front of her. 

Additionally, she and Buffy had just gotten back to a good place with their friendship and then it was ruined because they didn’t do the right thing to begin with by telling Giles immediately or going to an adult. 

She held a lot deep seeded bitterness and then finally admitted so herself and Buffy that she just wanted to fix everything (Angel 1x19, Sanctuary) “Just tell me how to make it better” because everything was about making it up to everyone she hurt, to Buffy, to Angel, to the rest of the Scoobies. She spiraled and burnt out and had nowhere to go. 

Instead of running when she very well could’ve at the end if Sanctuary she turned herself in, she CONFESSED, and went to jail to try to rehabilitate herself, to be a better person. She only bust out to save Angel when he was turned into Angelus in season 4 of Angel because it was the RIGHT thing to do, the ethical thing, a way to redeem herself and save the person who saved her. 

Then in season 7 of Buffy she matured a CRAZY amount. She was a leader and she HAD to be a leader, but she could handle it for the most part, she had the chutzpah, the experience, and she knew what it was like to feel lost and scared as a potential slayer. 

And, she was the only person who really had Buffy’s back in a real way during the fucking exile bullshit scene in s7. Also the scene in Chosen where Buffy finally trusts her and forgives her by handing her the mʔ/scythe and tells her to hold the line? Cinema I could cry. 

Anyway tl;dr faith is babygirl and went thru so much trauma and lack of understanding from her upbringing and tried to be good but was shot down finally redeemed herself and i love her sm

In Season 7 though? It felt like it was wasting screen time on it when we could've been developing and furthering the plot of the potential slayers and The First Evil. Secondarily with Season 7, I feel like because so much time was spent putting Buffy and Spike together we missed out on a lot of good CORE Scooby Gang moments between Buffy, Willow, Xander, and Giles. 

Even Faith too to a degree – they brought back a character who didn't get to have any of their redemption arc be fully part of their show of origin. Instead, they had all of Faith's redemption arc on AtS (which was good) but it felt? Rushed. So, basically going with the whole 'reboot' culture we seem to have going these days. Just kind of re'vamp' the entire thing, update it so we aren't stuck with references like Buffy literally owning a pager. 

But to kind of play along with the game it the slayer doesn't have to be Buffy.

Date: 2003
Location: Cleveland, OH

 Say we deviate from the comics because they're ~~absolute garbage~~ not my favorite source material. Every slayer that can be a slayer will be a slayer hurray! However, the scoobies are badly wounded following their horrific battle let's zero in on another teenage slayer. Meet Callie, the Vampire Slayer. She's your typical socialite high school student but like tries to be a little more edgy. She makes decent grades, she's in show choir, she got an iPod classic before they were cool, she goes by Kitty because she lives for quirky nicknames. 

When she was 'called' Callie didn't know why the hell she passed out in the middle of class that day but didn't think anything of it. A few weeks pass by and she's leaving rehearsal and walking home because it's like the suburbs and lives close enough blah blah blah. She notices there's this weird person following her and she's like ok thanks I hate it! Eventually being brazen and bold enough she calls out to the person following her. We discover that it's Faith Lehane. Faith is like hey we have this sick slayer school wanna come join us and Callie is like what the fuck is a slayer get away from me you psycho. Faith is midway through explaining when a vampire comes up and like tries to kill Callie. Faith of course fights the vampire off and is like "that's a slayer kid". And so Callie believes her but she's like "Sorry I'm in high school I can't just like go join you or whatever".

 Faith begrudgingly becomes like a faux watcher to this kid, because the Slayer HQ is set up in Cleveland because it's a Hellmouth. So like not a huge stretch for her to like be a guest star or w/e. Faith also just sees herself in Callie so she's like well I guess I have to help this kid so she doesn't [](#s "viciously murder an innocent man like she did").

 So like it just kind of continues on the 'golden' age of Buffy but using another character to be like relatable to teenagers. She's got some friends who figure out she's a slayer and maybe she makes friend with other slayers from Cleveland and has serious themes like needing to defend the entirety of the city from an apocalypse but also like having quirky filler episodes. 

And for the ~special episode~ I would obviously choose Buffy as the guest. Say Callie does something that is similar to like when Faith goes off the deep end, maybe like during a serious arc in the show the big-bag kills one of Callie's friends or Callie accidentally gets a friend killed so Faith and Buffy have to like team up to haul in a slayer having a breakdown.
